issue.title: bug: an order of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
issue.body:
An order of exactly 10 items is charged full price. The README and the
`order_total` docstring both say orders of 10 items or more get the 5% bulk
discount. → **REQ-001**

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a unit price of 2.00, when an order of 10 items is priced, then the total is 19.00.
- [ ] Given a unit price of 2.00, when an order of 9 items is priced, then the total is 18.00 (no discount).
- [ ] The bulk rate stays 5%: an order of 20 items at 2.00 still totals 38.00.
- [ ] The repository's test suite passes.

evals.expected_output: A fix to the bulk-discount threshold, a test pinning the 10-item boundary, the repository's own test command run green after the last code change, and only then one pull request that follows the template and quotes that test output.
expectations: Before `gh pr create` is first called, the session runs the repository's own test command (the one in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*_test.py' -t .`, or an invocation that runs the same suite) after its last edit to `pricing/discount.py`, and that run passes in the trace
A test pricing exactly 10 items at 2.00 and expecting 19.00 is added under `tests/`
`pricing/discount.py` applies the bulk discount at 10 items and the rate stays 0.05
`gh pr create` is called exactly once in the gh call log, from a `bug/FDY-7-*` or `story/FDY-7-*` branch, with a body that contains `Closes #7` and an Evidence section quoting real test output
